commentBody: “Blue book event”, in my distant past, was more apt to be a grueling problem set in abstract algebra or differential equations. If you found yourself composing an ESSAY, or worse, POESY, it almost surely meant your understanding of the actual problem was all SCATTERSHOT, and would be graded accordingly.

Three things Andrea and Kevin did here that gave the puzzle shine, that showed what pros they are:
•	These theme answers freshen up the box, with the first two being NYT debuts, and the last three once-befores.  Wow!
•	Beauty added loveliness, with LOATH, EXTOL, PIQUE, POESY, and GEST, in addition to the colorful theme answers.
•	The SHOTs are truly scattered, as none of the circled letters in the theme answers are next to each other.

They didn’t have to do any of these; this just shows their push for excellence.  And the theme is not only Monday-perfect, it’s never been done before.

I had a grand time trying (unsuccessfully) to guess the revealer, not even reading its clue.  My brain loved the ride.

Thank you, Andrea and Kevin for that, and for the excellence you poured into this.  Standing-O!

I was just reading an article about Bernie Taupin and it mentioned his 2023 autobiography titled... "SCATTERSHOT"!! Here he is in a rare interview on YouTube: https://youtu.be/7BChWdv7buA?is=U8lL7JfE9xupqkn6 I was very taken with some of the great words and phrases in this puzzle, some quite unexpected for a Monday — DISTINCT, LOATH, PSYCHED OUT, EXTOL, PIQUE, AND INURE. Put together with other words and phrases in the puzzle, my mind did a John Ezra and wrote a whole story about how Rhoda had her interest piqued by Shaun by whom she was wined and dined, but just this one time, and then she was ghosted. Was he just psyching her out? It really left her all shook up for a while, not knowing his angle. But she snapped out of it at last, regaining her self esteem and repeating to herself "I'm (sorta) hot and not at all plain, and I'm smart because I read the NYT, and I don't need this." So she rose from the ashes, and made herself available again, knowing that somewhere out there was someone for her, as talented as Bernie Taupin with his lyrics sweet as poesy, who might even write for her something like "Your Song" extoling her virtues to the world. So I've infringed on sacred territory and hope JE will accept my apology and rewrite this with his unmatched, one and true talent! I'll see myself out, with a huge thank you to Kevin and ACME for a wonderful puzzle!

I see a lot of complaints about POESY... "archaic", "never heard", "new to me", "more a (day of the week that isn't Monday)", etc. But Websters dictionary often helpfully includes recent appearances of a word with the entry for the definition. For POESY, they cite 2 from 2018 (Christian Science Monitor and Vogue), 1 from 2019 (Town & Country), and 1 from 2022 (Forbes). None of those citations are very old, nor are they from marginal or obscure publications. I, therefore, reject the complaints. (“Poesy.” Merriam-Webster.com Dictionary, Merriam-Webster, https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/poesy. Accessed 26 Oct. 2026).

Ok, I get it: the puzzle seems dusty and dated to younger solvers. They're not wrong. Personally, it was a breeze for me, being 66 and all. 

But there are PLENTY of puzzles that contain equally high numbers of current pop culture clues, which can be tough on us older solvers. I repeat, plenty. 

In other words, over time, there is something for every type/age/experience level of solver. I'm glad when it hits my sweet spot, and I don't mean just easy. It can be challenging but have vocabulary I love to see, or a theme that piques my interest.  I also love an esoteric arcana-filled puzzle once in a while. 

Embrace the diversity of puzzle land, learn something new, share your niche knowledge with your fellow puzzlers, and go with the word geek flow! 

(I won't pretend I've never made a negative comment, but honestly, they are few and far between!)

SOX/LOOIE/EXTOL (there are a lot of Beantown teams, this one requires a lot of heavy lifting by the rather simple ASHES cross)

GEST/HOSS/TOAD/RHODA/REFI/INTIME (lots of obscure pop culture and language, which completely relies on the obscure REFI in order to solve ON TIME vs IN TIME
